newEvidence.scope: Hot-runner startup/operation sequence and explicit requirement to follow machine-manufacturer documentation; applies to the covered Husky system, not all hot runners.

newEvidence.title: Hot Runner User Manual — System Startup and Shutdown
newEvidence.scope: System-specific startup/shutdown and thermally-sensitive-material cautions; evidence that procedures depend on system/material, not a universal recipe.

newEvidence.title: iQ weight control and iQ clamp control process monitoring guidance
newEvidence.scope: Application-specific adjustment of injection profile, switchover point, holding pressure and clamping force based on measured process signals; specific to ENGEL systems.

newEvidence.issuer: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
newEvidence.title: Assessment of fiber orientation models predictability by comparison with X-ray µCT data in injection-molded short glass fiber-reinforced polyamide
newEvidence.scope: Experimental X-ray micro-CT evidence that fibre orientation varies locally and materially affects properties and shrinkage/warpage-related defects in short-glass-fibre-reinforced injection mouldings.

resolutions.reason: Two independent hot-runner manufacturers document heated-system startup/operation as system-specific. The chapter wording must remain generic and must not import either supplier's numeric procedure.
Manufacturer manual explicitly treats thermally sensitive material and staged hot-runner heating as system/material dependent. No universal temperature/residence threshold is permitted.
Manufacturer manuals provide explicit startup/shutdown instructions and Husky explicitly directs users to machine-manufacturer documentation. Installed-system documentation remains controlling.

ENGEL demonstrates application-specific clamping-force determination from mould breathing, supporting the claim that one generic projected-area rule is insufficient. This does not establish a universal sizing method.

ENGEL shows switchover point is actively adjusted using process signals as conditions change, corroborating that transfer is process-dependent. It remains vendor-specific evidence, so the generic establishment method is not promoted to fully supported.

Peer-reviewed experimental work directly links fibre orientation distribution in injection-moulded reinforced thermoplastics with mechanical properties and shrinkage/warpage-related defects; chapter wording remains scoped to reinforced systems.
